rationale: The Court is likely to issue a relatively narrow express-preemption opinion under FIFRA §136v(b) and Bates, emphasizing that a Missouri verdict effectively compelling a glyphosate cancer warning after EPA’s repeated consideration and approval of a label without it imposes an “additional or different” labeling requirement. Separate writings are most likely from the dissenters (pressing Wyeth/Albrecht-style clarity concerns) and from one or more textualist conservatives (to underscore that the analysis rests on express preemption rather than implied-impossibility frameworks).
